title: Moduli categories viewed over a smaller base and their absolute diagonal
statement: Let $S,B$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $g:S\to B$. Write $j_g:\mathit{Sch}/S\to\mathit{Sch}/B$ for composition with $g$. For a category $p_F:F\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ and functors and natural transformations over $S$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], define $g_!F$ to have the same total category $F$ and projection $j_g\circ p_F$. A functor $f:F\to G$ over $S$ induces $g_!f:g_!F\to g_!G$ with the same underlying functor. The canonical projection from $g_!F$ to the category $\mathit{Sch}/S$ regarded over $B$ is $p_F$. For an $S$-scheme $U$, the canonical scheme-chart comparison $g_!h_U\to h_{j_g(U)}$ sends each map $T\to U$ and each commuting triangle to the same scheme maps, now over $B$. The category of morphisms of pairs $(g_!F,p_F)\to(g_!G,p_G)$ is the full subcategory of functors over $B$ satisfying $p_G\circ f=p_F$, with their natural transformations over $B$. Using the affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum], for $B=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $g$ the unique map, define the absolute product of $F,G$ to be the existing $2$-fibre product [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] of their changed projections to the base category $\mathit{Sch}/B$ with its identity projection. Define the absolute diagonal of $F$ using the relative diagonal [def-sfb-dm-stack-morphism-properties] of its changed structural projection; it sends $x$ to $(x,x,\mathrm{id})$. These constructions impose no algebraicity, separation or finiteness assumption.
